Question: How does the platform abstract auth complexity across different Okta grant types (OAuth 2.0 AuthCode, Client Credentials, SAML-bridged, PKCE, device flow, service accounts)? Describe credential vault, automatic token refresh, on-behalf-of flows, and agent vs user identity separation.
Response: Auth complexity is fully abstracted at the platform level — agent developers never manage tokens. APIM AI Gateway handles auth injection for all MCP tool calls. For each MCP server registered in APIM, the auth configuration is defined once: grant type, client credentials, scopes, token endpoint. APIM injects the appropriate auth header into every tool call. Supported grant types: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code (LinkedIn), Client Credentials (service-to-service), SAML-bridged via Okta (Workday), PKCE (web portal), Device Flow, OBO (Graph API on behalf of human). Credential vault: Azure Key Vault stores all secrets with Entra RBAC access control. Automated credential rotation via Key Vault policies without agent downtime — APIM picks up rotated credentials automatically. OBO flows: when a human triggers an action, the agent executor acquires an OBO token using the human's delegated permissions. Agent vs user identity: Entra Agent ID distinguishes agent actions (app-only) from human-delegated actions (OBO). Audit trail attributes each action to the correct identity. Prompt-injection hardening: tool calls from GHCP SDK sessions carry JWT claims (skill ID, version, workflow phase, jurisdiction) issued by the Hosted Agent's managed identity; APIM validates these claims against the per-skill tool allow-list at the gateway — a prompt-injected attempt to elevate capability (call a tool not in the current skill's allow-list) is rejected before reaching the backend. All auth injection occurs inside the Private Endpoint boundary; APIM is the sole public edge.
Key Technologies: APIM AI Gateway (auth injection + JWT claim validation + per-skill allow-list), Azure Key Vault (CMK + auto-rotation), Entra Agent ID (phishing-resistant MFA on humans; managed identity for agents), Azure Private Endpoints, Okta federation via Entra External ID, OBO flows
POC Demo: POC1: Show seamless auth across Workday (SAML-bridged), D365 (native), and Maconomy (API key) — agent developer sees none of the auth complexity.

Question: Describe your approach to bridging REST/OpenAPI APIs into MCP-compatible tool definitions: auto-generation, parameter mapping, auth injection, response transformation. Build-time or runtime?
Response: APIM AI Gateway provides the REST-to-MCP gateway runtime, with Azure API Center as the discoverable registry. Build-time process: (1) Import an OpenAPI spec into APIM. (2) APIM auto-generates MCP tool definitions from the API operations — each operation becomes a typed MCP tool with parameter mapping derived from the OpenAPI schema. (3) The auto-generated tool definitions are registered in API Center with full metadata (capabilities, owning team, lifecycle stage, supported environments, cross-cloud origin) so other agents can discover them. (4) Configure auth injection (which credential from Key Vault, which grant type). (5) Configure response transformation if needed (extract relevant fields from verbose API responses). (6) The MCP tool is immediately available to GHCP SDK sessions inside MAF agent executors that discover tools through API Center / APIM. Runtime: tool discovery (API Center catalog), auth injection, rate limiting, and content safety are runtime operations handled by APIM. The auto-generated MCP tool definitions can be customised post-generation (rename tools, add descriptions, adjust parameter mappings). All governed through APIM policies and API Center lifecycle gates. This same pattern applies to Databricks SQL Warehouse, Snowflake, Mosaic AI Gateway, and Snowflake Cortex — their OpenAPI surfaces are bridged to MCP tools via the REST-to-MCP gateway, exposing WPP's existing analytics data and fine-tuned models for agent consumption without migration.
Key Technologies: APIM REST-to-MCP gateway, Azure API Center (registry, discovery, lifecycle), OpenAPI import, Azure Key Vault (auth), APIM policies (governance)
POC Demo: POC1: Live demo — import Maconomy OpenAPI spec into APIM, auto-generate MCP tools, a MAF agent executor (GHCP SDK session) discovers and invokes them.

Question: Describe the full dev/test/staging/production lifecycle for agents and tools: version control, promotion workflows, approval gates, rollback, environment-specific configuration.
Response: Full lifecycle management across all artefacts. Skills: Git-committed SKILL.md files synced to Azure API Center. Lifecycle stages: Design -> Preview -> Production -> Deprecated. Promotion requires approval gates in CI/CD. Each environment (dev/staging/prod) has its own API Center configuration. Rollback by promoting a previous version. MCP servers: source code in Git, deployed via CI/CD (Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions) to per-environment APIM instances. Environment-specific configuration (dev uses sandbox APIs, production uses live systems). APIM policies: version-controlled via APIOps CI/CD. Per-environment policy sets. PR review gates for changes. Instant rollback via deployment slot swap. Durable Functions orchestrations: deployed via CI/CD with environment-specific connection strings and configurations. Deployment slots for zero-downtime updates. Models: per-environment model deployments in Foundry. Production uses pinned model versions. Staging can test new model versions.
Key Technologies: Azure API Center lifecycle, APIOps CI/CD, Git, Azure DevOps/GitHub Actions, deployment slots, Foundry model deployments
POC Demo: POC1: Show full promotion workflow — skill in Design, tested in staging, promoted to Production with approval gate.

Question: Describe the centralised tool catalogue: metadata (description, auth requirements, rate limits, SLA, owning team, supported environments). Can agents discover tools dynamically?
Response: APIM AI Gateway maintains the centralised tool catalog. Each registered MCP server carries rich metadata: description of capabilities, auth requirements (grant type, scopes), rate limits (per-agent, per-environment), SLA expectations, owning team, supported environments (dev/staging/prod), and data classification. Dynamic discovery: GHCP SDK sessions inside MAF agent executors discover available MCP tools through APIM at session start. The skill declares which tool categories it needs; APIM returns available tools matching the declaration. This enables tool evolution without skill changes — if a new Workday API version is deployed as a new MCP server, skills that declare 'Workday HR data' tools will discover the updated version. The Control Plane UI provides a browsable tool catalog for operators and developers.
Key Technologies: APIM AI Gateway tool catalog, MCP tool discovery, metadata management

Question: Describe integration with enterprise secrets management (Azure Key Vault, HashiCorp Vault). How is automated credential rotation handled without agent downtime?
Response: Azure Key Vault is the primary secrets management platform. All credentials (API keys, certificates, client secrets, connection strings) are stored in Key Vault with Entra RBAC access control. Automated rotation: Key Vault supports auto-rotation policies for certificates and secrets. When a credential rotates, APIM picks up the new version automatically via Key Vault reference — no agent restart, no downtime, no code change. The rotation is logged in Key Vault audit logs. For MCP servers: APIM injects credentials at request time by referencing Key Vault named values. Rotation is transparent to both the MCP server and the agent executor. For Okta tokens: APIM handles token refresh automatically — if a cached token expires, APIM re-authenticates using credentials from Key Vault. HashiCorp Vault: if WPP uses HashiCorp Vault, Azure Key Vault can sync secrets from external vaults via Key Vault's external secret store support. Key Vault supports Customer-Managed Keys (CMK) encryption at rest and double encryption for high-assurance workloads. MFA on Key Vault access is enforced via Entra Conditional Access with phishing-resistant methods only (FIDO2, Windows Hello, Authenticator with number matching) — SMS and voice blocked. Agent runtime never sees raw credentials — APIM injects at request time.
Key Technologies: Azure Key Vault (CMK, auto-rotation, double encryption option), APIM Key Vault references, Entra RBAC + Conditional Access (phishing-resistant MFA)

Question: Describe fine-grained control: which agents access which tools, with what permissions, in which environments. Rate limiting per agent, data classification constraints.
Response: Fine-grained tool access control at three levels. (1) APIM policies: per-agent, per-tool, per-environment access rules. The Hiring Agent identity can access Greenhouse MCP but not D365 Finance MCP. Production environment restricts tools that staging allows. Rate limiting configured per agent per tool — prevent a single agent from overwhelming an external API. (2) GHCP SDK hooks: tool allowlisting per skill — if a skill's SKILL.md doesn't declare a tool, the onPreToolUse hook blocks the call and logs the violation. This prevents prompt injection from tricking an agent into calling unauthorised tools. (3) Entra RBAC: the Hosted Agent's Entra identity has scoped permissions on downstream resources — even if a tool call bypassed APIM and hooks (which it cannot), Entra RBAC on the target system would deny access. Data classification: Purview data classification labels flow through APIM — tools accessing classified data enforce the classification constraints. 4-class data model enforced across the platform (Workflow state / Model context / Audit ledger / Telemetry) with distinct residency, retention, and redaction — e.g. model context is ephemeral and Guardrails-redacted on egress, audit ledger is immutable 7-12y in Log Analytics, telemetry in App Insights never carries prompt bodies. Per-skill tool allow-list compiled into APIM policy fragment at skill promotion — APIM rejects skill-to-tool violations at the gateway (enforcement outside the agent runtime, cannot be bypassed by the LLM).
Key Technologies: APIM per-agent/per-skill/per-tool policies, GHCP SDK hooks (tool allowlisting), Entra RBAC, Purview data classification, 4-class data model
POC Demo: POC2: Show tool access control — Hiring Agent's skill tries to access Finance MCP tool, hook blocks the call, violation logged.
